# euija — #64–#71 rewrite notes

Patch: `scripts/.cache/rewrite/euija.mjs` (idempotent; each episode skips itself once its marker text exists). `validate.mjs 64 71` → ok. Anchors: 0 unmatched in range (baseline had 11; all fixed, none added).

## #64 Coup (re-dated 657)
- Proclamation cut from six blocks to two and cross-cut with the room (a cough, Chunbok's ink whisper, Minister Satek's "For how long?"). "Deer Rock" → the Rock of Politics (text + diagram title).
- Chunbok's turn staged live: the young man who whispered "he's lost his mind" raises the first sleeve. Cut the after-the-fact summary, the staged "Satek lackey" line and the 657 record.
- New Gyebek beat: that night Euija writes the recall himself; Chunbok talks him into "a month"; the letter goes into his sleeve (pays off in #65, #66, #70). One narrator line on Chunbok's double game before Chang'an.
- First line kept (B). Card kept, 17 words: "He beat eight houses in one morning. Now he can't sleep. In his dreams, somebody keeps counting…?"

## #65 Descent (re-dated 657 September)
- The thirteen shot-list paragraphs are now three storyteller paragraphs ("The stories say three thousand"; "Here is what the lamps do not show"). About 80 image anchors re-pointed to the new text.
- Cut the textbook paranoia line. Heungsu gets a live scene before his exile (Diamond Sutra; Euija interrupts: "I can read a map").
- Chunbok's yearly "bring back Gyebek" is framed as a small tax; the letter is still in the sleeve when Euija says "That… who?".
- The arrest is spelled out ("Take his belt"), the duplicate record is cut, the "hollow ring" wording is gone, Sungchung spelled one way in the narration. The memorial ends under a wine jar (sets up #68).
- First line kept (B). Card kept, 24 words.

## #66 Nine Omens
- Numbered list and annals widget replaced by one told version (two paragraphs); the shaman's reading is now the interpretation. Cut the second shaman intro and the Yamato record; the shout comes before the blade.
- Muyeol flashback opened by Euija pricing the turtle ("Who buried you, little one?"). Fixed "took the throne" → "a prince on a mudbank", "sent away" → "a letter he never sent to the man he never sent for". Moved the stage direction out of his line.
- Required lead-in: on the riverbank Chunbok voices the doubt (will there be a Baekje for him to come home to?); Euija: "We were a younger son's house… Goguryeo got the hall. We got the road south."
- First line (D→A): "Every one of the nine signs is real, in the sense that people saw it."
- Card, 23 words: "Will Baekje survive? To answer that, go back to how it began: a mother, two sons, and a father who already had one…!"

## #67 Onjo
- New hook, then the existing scenes. Lady Ye's speech is now in objects. Cleared up the #39 shorthand. The last night is new, not a rerun ("I'll count. You know I'm bad at it." / "Say the thing you never say").
- Cut the spoiler summary and both records. New ending makes the kinship plain (Yuri keeps the chair, Onjo takes the river: "one father's sons… one got the hall, one got the road") and returns to Euija wringing out his sleeves: "This was the story."
- First line: "Every child in Baekje can tell you this story. Most of them get the beginning wrong."
- Card, 23 words: "Back to Sabi. Two armies are on the road, the boat for Gyebek still hasn't sailed, and the king wants to know why…!"

## #68 Sungchung (stub of ~200 words grown to ~800)
- Built into a full episode. Euija holds court sober, finds out Chunbok sat on the boat for a year, and sends it. That night he finds Sungchung's page under the wine jar and has a maid read it. Chimhyeon is glossed as Tanhyeon here, once. The page brings him to Heungsu. Ye Sikjin is asked for men and promises "as many as the road allows", then opens his drawer. Cut the news summary, the Red Fowl record and the floating aphorism.
- First line (C→A): "The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first."
- Card kept (A), 16 words.

## #69 Heungsu
- First line (C→A): "Heungsu has drawn the same map in the dirt every morning for three years. Today the king has finally sent someone to look at it."
- The berth flashback (655) is now Gyebek's **exile**, not a march. Heungsu sees him off, and so do **his wife, his boy and a small girl**. The boy asks how many days to Tamla ("Count to five. The wind is not always good."). The wife overhears "the same person" and does not look surprised. A courier's line opens the flashback ("Has anybody sent for Gyebek?").
- The ministers' record is now a scene: Chunbok, a minister, and the "chickens in a basket" trap. Euija has a reason to agree: taking the advice would mean admitting what it cost Sungchung. Cut the record that repeated Heungsu's line. The ring is gone.
- Card kept (B), 21 words.

## #70 Gyebek
- The family are planted on the island (he counts to five for a boy the island can't see). The boat brings Euija's own words ("The river was cold. I went in. Come home.").
- **The Euija–Gyebek scene**: a reunion in the palace yard. Euija confesses the unsent letter, and Gyebek quotes "Judge it yourself" back word for word. Gyebek says "I gave my word", which is the line #72 should echo. "You asked me once whether I liked the name, or you… Both." At the gate, Euija offers Bear Fortress for the family; Gyebek answers "If Sabi falls, no wall in Baekje is thick", and Euija says "Then judge it yourself."
- The yard before the killing: the wife, and the son counting ("Was it right?" / "Yes."). The act stays offstage. Cut the MORAL. "Raised me" became the naming. Added one beat of the five thousand at the crossroads.
- First line kept (A). Card, 22 words: "Somewhere, Kangrim closes his ledger on a swept yard. Then he goes up to a meeting with one question he shouldn't ask…!"

## #71 Three Realms
- Dropped the "Epilogue · Part II" label and the 정자 in the English. Cut the gossip to five lines and dropped the "thing" grudge, the crucifixion joke and the stage directions.
- Kangrim's resurrection question now has a cause. That morning he collected Gyebek's wife and children, and the girl asked whether her father was coming ("Later."). Hallakgungi shuts it down ("pick a flower for one mortal and the whole row wilts"). Kangrim opens the Yellow Mountain page. Logline updated.
- First line (D→A): "Once a year the gods hold a meeting. Kangrim is late to this one, because of a yard in Baekje."
- Card kept, 18 words, still into #72.
